findings.title: Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `retryCount > 1` branch is an OR condition without a `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint. Consequently, any non-SMS `WorkflowReminder` (for example, email or WhatsApp) whose retryCount exceeds one will be permanently deleted by this SMS cron endpoint, even though this job neither schedules nor owns those reminder types. Keep the retry threshold inside an SMS-scoped condition so this destructive cleanup cannot remove unrelated workflow reminder records.

findings.title: Retry counts can be lost when cron executions overlap
findings.body: The retry value is read in `findMany` and then written back as `reminder.retryCount + 1`. If two authorized cron invocations process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both can read (for example) 0 and both write 1 after failures. The row will then receive an extra retry despite two failed scheduling attempts, so the intended two-attempt limit is not enforced (and concurrent executions can continue submitting duplicate provider requests). Use an atomic database increment and/or atomically claim the reminder before scheduling; the catch-path update at line 195 has the same lost-update issue.

findings.title: Reminders with no sendable message or recipient never consume retries
findings.body: RetryCount is incremented only after `scheduleSMS` returns false or throws. When `message` is empty/null or `sendTo` is absent, the condition at this line is skipped entirely, leaving the reminder `scheduled: false` and `retryCount` unchanged. The cron will select and reprocess that permanently unsendable reminder on every run until its scheduled date, which preserves the retry loop this change is intended to stop. Mark these cases as failed attempts (or delete/cancel them explicitly) so they are bounded by the same retry policy.
